context:
RESULT (merged in PR 3310, record _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md on develop). Committed harness _project/scripts/tpchavoc_trino_q1_scale_check.py, measured at a clean tree 50147781, Trino 484. The first run measured the earlier CROSS JOIN UNNEST text; develop #3326 then changed 1_v7 on Presto/Trino/Athena to the fork's order_list_aggregates + reduce_list_aggregates rewrites (four ordered ARRAY_AGG columns reduced with REDUCE/ZIP_WITH), so those numbers were discarded and everything was re-measured on the current text.

Stock limits (6 GiB heap, query.max-memory-per-node 1.80 GB = 1843 MiB): SF1 PASS 795-820 MiB (<=45% of cap); SF2 PASS 1590-1595 MiB (87% of cap); SF3 and SF10 FAIL EXCEEDED_LOCAL_MEMORY_LIMIT (HashAggregationOperator 1.63 GB = the four ARRAY_AGG states). Raised limits (8 GiB heap, 6 GB cap): SF1 823-833, SF2 1522-1595, SF3 2393, SF5 3897 MiB; all equal to canonical Q1 (max relative difference <=5.3e-11; integer counts exact). Memory is linear in rows, 760-835 MiB per SF. Canonical Q1 <=16 MiB. Limits BIND from SF3 on stock Trino; acceptance bullet 1 is met at SF1 (and SF2).

Harness defects found in oracle review and fixed before merge: integer cells now compared exactly (not with the float tolerance), NaN/Infinity cells never equivalent, tree state is null when git fails and git runs in the script's repository. A replay at f305695a (raised limits, SF1-SF5) reproduced every number.

REMEDY SPEC (acceptance bullet 2; no product code changed). Candidate probe, run on the EARLIER UNNEST text on Trino 476 with a throwaway script that was NOT committed: single runs, SF3 unless noted, results equal to canonical within ~3e-11, peaks noisy (+/-25% between runs of one query), so only large effects mean anything. Baseline 4 ordered ARRAY_AGG 2267-2377 MiB (SF5 4378). Chunking via GROUP BY (flag, status, l_orderkey/2097152): 2282 MiB, no reduction because a hash aggregation holds every group before emitting. UNION ALL of 4 l_orderkey-range slices: 2271 MiB, no reduction because branches run concurrently. ONE ARRAY_AGG of ROW(q,p,d,t) ORDER BY l_orderkey,l_linenumber: 1226-1435 MiB (SF5 2322), about 0.5-0.6x baseline. Same without ORDER BY: 1075 MiB (SF5 2658), within noise of the ordered form. The hash-aggregation state is the same under the current REDUCE text (same four ARRAY_AGGs; memory per SF matches the earlier text), so the same factor is plausible, but it has NOT been re-tested against the REDUCE rendering.
SPEC: (1) replace the four positionally aligned arrays with one array of ROW values, and re-measure with this harness at a clean recorded commit before claiming a gain. The rewrite lives in the fork's list-aggregate rewrites reached through translate_list_aggregate_variant / list_aggregate_variant_rewrites in benchbox/core/tpchavoc/dialect_compat.py, so the change is a fork or rule change plus a BenchBox pin. (2) It is NOT a bounded-memory fix: every single-statement form that materialises a group's rows as arrays is O(rows in the largest group), and Q1 has only four group keys so a cluster cannot divide the largest group. Say so in the variant description. Expected effect if the factor holds: stock-limit break moves from SF3 to about SF5-SF6 (extrapolated). (3) Decide with the owner whether 1_v7 on Presto/Trino needs a documented memory requirement or a scale-gated skip; skip rules are keyed by platform, not scale, so verify that mechanism first.

STILL UNKNOWN: Presto C++ behaviour. The current text uses REDUCE, and Presto C++ is reported to cap REDUCE input at 100,000 elements, which a Q1 group exceeds at any scale above about SF0.02; #3326 checked PrestoDB only at TPC-H tiny scale (tracked in tpchavoc-native-engine-verification). Also unmeasured: multi-node memory split; SF>5 on raised limits. Wall time: 1_v7 took 17-22 s at SF3 and 30-42 s at SF5 on raised limits in the final run (an earlier run on a loaded machine took 57-127 s); with the earlier UNNEST text at about 14 s at SF3 on Trino 476 there is no clear evidence of a slowdown, so no controlled-comparison item was filed.
description: The Q1 DuckDB-LIST to ARRAY_AGG+UNNEST rewrite was motivated by the Presto C++ 100,000-element REDUCE limit, but neither the old limit nor the new ARRAY_AGG ... ORDER BY memory behavior was tested at scale: the Trino 476 smoke could not load SF1 lineitem (memory-connector 128MiB limit) and ran only tpch tiny. A scale run needs a Trino deployment with a real connector (not the memory connector) or a native Presto cluster. This is correctness-adjacent performance verification, not a known failure.
